mainTopic: A disputed boat: should בית דין seize property while one side looks for witnesses, and should it release the property if no witnesses come? Then the rule of כל דאלים גבר when each side says 'it was my ancestors'', and how that differs from two deeds dated the same day.
overview: Two people each claim the same boat. One of them asks בית דין to hold it until he brings witnesses. רב הונא says בית דין holds it, and רב יהודה says it does not. When he finds no witnesses, he asks בית דין to let the boat go so that whoever is stronger wins. רב יהודה says it is not released, and רב פפא says it is. The הלכה is that בית דין does not seize, but once something is seized, it is not released. Next, רב נחמן rules כל דאלים גבר when each side says the property came from his ancestors. The גמרא then starts asking how this is different from two שטרות issued on the same day, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two people fight over a boat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells a story: two people each claim a boat is theirs. One of them asks בית דין to hold the boat until he brings witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a boat that two people were fighting over. Each said, 'It's mine.' One of them went to court and said: 'Take hold of it until I bring witnesses that it's mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a case. Nothing has been decided yet; it is preparing the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side has proof, and neither side has a clear חזקה on the boat. One side wants בית דין to step in and hold the boat for now, so the other side can't take it while he looks for witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Seize it / take hold of it

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא אַרְבָּא דַּהֲווֹ מִינְּצוּ עֲלַהּ בֵּי תְרֵי,
phrases.english: There was a certain boat that two people were quarreling over.
This one said: "It is mine,"
and that one said: "It is mine."

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ לְבֵי דִינָא, וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: One of them came to the court and said:
Seize it until I bring witnesses that it is mine.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא אַרְבָּא דַּהֲווֹ מִינְּצוּ עֲלַהּ בֵּי תְרֵי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A case is presented: two people each claim a boat, and one asks בית דין to hold it while he gets witnesses.

steps.title: Does the court hold the boat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether בית דין should take hold of the boat at his request.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we take hold of it, or don't we?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the main question of this case: should בית דין step in and hold the boat for now?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether one side's promise to bring witnesses is enough reason for בית דין to get involved before any proof exists.

phrases.english: Do we seize it, or do we not seize it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the legal question that comes out of the case in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בית דין holds disputed property at one claimant's request while he looks for witnesses.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב יהודה disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says בית דין holds the boat. רב יהודה says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: We take hold of it. רב יהודה said: We don't take hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא lets בית דין protect the claim while proof is on the way. רב יהודה says that without proof yet, בית דין has no reason to step in.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא; here he says we do seize
An אמורא; here he says we don't seize

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: We seize it.
Rav Yehuda said: We do not seize it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with two opposite opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: בית דין seizes. רב יהודה: בית דין does not seize.

steps.title: No witnesses found: should the court let go?
steps.stepSummary: The man finds no witnesses and asks בית דין to release the boat so that whoever is stronger can win. The גמרא asks whether בית דין releases it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and didn't find witnesses. He told the court: 'Let it go, and whoever is stronger wins.' Do we let it go, or don't we?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. The boat is already in בית דין's hands, the witnesses never came, and the גמרא asks a new question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without proof or a חזקה, the default rule is כל דאלים גבר, meaning the stronger side wins. The question is whether בית דין, once it is holding the boat, should hand it back to that free-for-all.

keyTerms.meaning: We release / take out of the court's hands

phrases.english: He went, and did not find witnesses.
He said to them: Release it,
and whoever is stronger prevails.
Do we release it, or do we not release it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same story into a second stage and asks a second question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Once בית דין holds the disputed property and no proof comes, does it release the property so that the stronger side wins?

steps.title: רב יהודה and רב פפא disagree about releasing
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says בית דין does not release the boat. רב פפא says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: We don't let it go. רב פפא said: We do let it go.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers about releasing the boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה holds that once בית דין is holding the boat, it stays there. רב פפא holds that once no proof comes, the reason for holding it is gone, so בית דין lets it go.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא; here he says we release

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: We do not release it.
Rav Pappa said: We release it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה: we do not release. רב פפא: we release.

steps.title: The הלכה: don't seize, but once seized, don't release
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that בית דין does not seize disputed property, but if it was already seized, בית דין does not release it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: we don't take hold of it. But if it was already taken, we don't let it go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling for both questions about the boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On seizing, the הלכה follows רב יהודה: בית דין doesn't step in. On releasing, it follows the view that what is already held stays held. So the ruling sides with רב יהודה on both questions.
steps.whatToRemember: Two rules: (1) בית דין does not seize disputed property just because one side promises witnesses. (2) If it was already seized, בית דין does not release it to כל דאלים גבר.
steps.confusionAlert: These two rules don't contradict each other. 'Don't seize' is about starting to hold the boat; 'don't release' is about a boat that is already being held.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: We do not seize,
and where it was seized, we do not release it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles both disputes from steps 3 and 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We don't seize; but once seized, we don't release.

steps.title: Both say 'my ancestors': whoever is stronger wins
steps.stepSummary: Each side says the property came to him from his ancestors. רב נחמן rules כל דאלים גבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One says: 'It was my fathers'.' The other says: 'It was my fathers'.' רב נחמן said: Whoever is stronger wins.
steps.whatsHappening: A new case: each side claims he inherited the property. רב נחמן says בית דין doesn't decide; the stronger side keeps it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side has proof or a חזקה, and each claim is just as strong as the other. So בית דין stays out, and the property goes to whoever can take hold of it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the ruling here

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the rule כל דאלים גבר when two claims are exactly even.

phrases.english: This one says: "It was my ancestors',"
and that one says: "It was my ancestors'" –

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כֹּל דְּאַלִּים גָּבַר.
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: Whoever is stronger prevails.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר: ״שֶׁל אֲבוֹתַי״, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר: ״שֶׁל אֲבוֹתַי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case on the same theme of a dispute with no proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both sides claim inheritance with no proof, כל דאלים גבר.

steps.title: How is this different from two deeds on the same day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רב נחמן by comparing his case to two שטרות dated the same day. The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from two documents that come out on the same day...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against רב נחמן's ruling. The sentence is not finished here; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two deeds for the same field with the same date are also an even tie. If בית דין gives a ruling there instead of leaving it to the stronger side, why not here too? The rest of the question and the answer come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (opens a challenge)
Two documents (deeds of sale or gift)
That are issued on the same day

phrases.english: And what is different from two deeds
phrases.notes: He means two deeds of sale or gift for the same field.

phrases.english: that are issued on one day –

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִשְּׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת הַיּוֹצְאִין בְּיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling from step 7 by comparing it to a similar case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule of כל דאלים גבר in step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two deeds dated the same day are also an even tie, and that case seems to be handled differently. So why should כל דאלים גבר apply here?
